dimensions.note: key and password are sensitive; a PEM reaches cosign only as COSIGN_KEY in the subprocess environment, the passphrase as COSIGN_PASSWORD; argv shows <pem> in errors and the PEM is masked in everything cosign prints; the passphrase is not masked on purpose, cosign never prints it and a short one would mangle parsed output (found by the live test). generateKeyPair records the private key as a sensitive field.
Every method logs intent and outcome with structured placeholders; no secret is logged; the fingerprint, not the key, identifies the public key.

Tags, bad annotations, an empty key, an unreadable predicate or file are refused before cosign runs; a verification that fails is a record with cosign's reason, any other cosign failure throws before writing; JSON cosign prints is checked before use; a public key whose PEM body is not base64 is named as such; a CRLF PEM is accepted as cosign accepts it.

26 unit tests with a fake cosign cover describe, generateKeyPair, sign, verify, attest, verifyAttestation, signBlob, verifyBlob, masking, CRLF PEMs, name uniqueness, the parsers and the checks; the COSIGN_E2E test ran cosign 3.1.4 against a throwaway registry: key pair, sign, verify, wrong key, attest, verify-attestation, blob signed, verified and tampered; the two workflows and @dataverket/ko-signed-images ran live with a vaulted key.

sign, attest and signBlob are additive: a second run adds a signature or rewrites the bundle, nothing is lost; temporary files (signing config, public key, key pair, bundle paths) are removed in finally.
No HTTP of its own; the contract is cosign 3.1.4's CLI, whose JSON output and exit codes the tests pin.
Scratch removes every temporary file on every path; stdin is closed so cosign cannot prompt; subprocesses take the context signal.
README, skill and tests use registry.example.org, example PEMs and 127.0.0.1:5000 for the throwaway registry; no real infrastructure named.

Closed z.object schemas throughout; every hash field, the signer's fingerprint, a predicate's and a file's sha256, has the sha256: prefix; keypair.passphraseSet says whether a passphrase was given, since cosign's PEM is always an encrypted block.
Every resource spec declares lifetime infinite and garbageCollection 10.
A signature is not a managed resource: created and verified, never updated or deleted here.

arguments (policy), cosign-installed (local, live) and key-usable (live, before sign, attest and signBlob); an auto-definition's vault text fails arguments by design, with a message saying to run the workflow.

signer, keypair, <spec>-<repository, sanitized>-<12 hex of digest> and <blob spec>-<file name>-<12 hex of the path's sha256> never collide across specs; one digest in two repositories, or two files of one name in two directories, give two records, as a test proves.
No method reads stored data back.
